title: Reworking QuerySet.order_by() validation dropped the ORDER_PATTERN regex check for strings containing a period, so a 'table.column'-style value from request input is passed through as raw SQL in ORDER BY.

findings.explanation: The fix attempts to guard the 'dot-in-item' branch with ORDER_PATTERN.match(), but the logic change is subtle and potentially incomplete. Previously any string containing '.' triggered the deprecated raw-column-alias warning path. Now only strings matching ORDER_PATTERN (r'[-+]?[.\w]+$') AND containing '.' reach that branch. However, strings that do NOT match ORDER_PATTERN and DO contain '.' will silently fall through to whatever the else/default handling is — which may allow injection via paths like 'table.column; DROP TABLE'. The test added ('queries.name);') exercises the FieldError path, suggesting the non-matching case is caught elsewhere, but the exact flow of the else-branch is not visible in this diff. The fix is also only applied to the warning branch, not necessarily to the query-building branch. Confidence is moderate because the full query-building logic is not shown.

findings.suggested_fix: Ensure that ORDER_PATTERN is used to validate ALL order_by string inputs before they are used to construct SQL, not just the dot-containing deprecation branch. Reject or raise an error for any item that does not match the pattern.

findings.explanation: This change is purely in the ORM query-building layer and does not touch any authorization, authentication, or access-control logic. No endpoint, view, or permission check is modified.
